thread.title: 2026 Workforce Summit calls for closer alignment between higher education and industry

author: a. m. egan
title: 2026 Workforce Summit calls for closer alignment between higher education and industry
text:
Sandra Gilot-West, chief of staff for the Office of the Secretary of Higher Education, said on May 6 that New Jersey will need a workforce with more postsecondary education or training by 2031. She spoke at the 2026 Workforce Summit presented by Focus NJ and the New Jersey Business & Industry Association.
Gilot-West said that “higher education is being asked to be more responsive, more connected, and more outcomes-driven.” She added, “This underscores the partnership we need to have between higher education and industry to prepare the next generation of talent and to continue to provide upskilling opportunities to the current workforce.”
She described several state programs aimed at meeting these goals. One example is the New Jersey Career Accelerator Internship Grant Program, which provides grants for employers in New Jersey to offer paid training experiences for students and recent graduates.
The summit’s focus on collaboration comes as projections show that about 68% of jobs in New Jersey will require some form of postsecondary education or training within five years. The event highlighted ongoing efforts by business groups such as the New Jersey Business & Industry Association—which serves as the nation’s largest statewide employer association representing private-sector employers throughout New Jersey—to connect businesses with educational institutions according to the official website.
The association facilitates partnerships among businesses, government entities, and academic institutions while offering advocacy, information resources, cost-saving benefits, and support for business prosperity according to its official website. Michele Siekerka serves as president and chief executive officer according to its official website.
Gilot-West concluded her remarks by emphasizing that co-investment in talent development remains critical for preparing both new entrants into the workforce and providing upskilling opportunities.
